ORCHESTRATOR Step 5c -- audit_batch WARNs explained, and both are properties of the RESPONSE DATA, not itemtext defects. (a) Row-count anomaly on maser_lang_para/_stry/_vilname/_word1/_word2 vs median 17409: the ASER instrument is a skip ladder (a mother who cannot read letters is not asked to read words), and the story and village-name items exist only on the endline form. Re-checked server-side via item_stats.R: baseline n=8857 and endline n=8552 for every universally-administered item (8857+8552=17409 exactly), vilname n=8552 at endline only, and the ladder falls monotonically. (b) Blank option_text on maser_lang_lttrs/_word1/_word2: those three were COUNTS in the source form and reach IRW as 0/1 through an upstream dichotomisation whose threshold is documented nowhere in the deposit, so no honest label attaches to 0 or 1.

ORCHESTRATOR Step 5b -- the agent's claim of an undocumented upstream dichotomisation was re-checked independently and is CORROBORATED by a number the agent did not use. If the 0/1 cut on maser_lang_lttrs were the ASER pass-to-advance criterion, the number advancing to word1 would match the number scoring 1 on lttrs; it does not. At endline, lttrs has n=8552 with mean 0.12 (about 1,026 mothers scoring 1), yet 3,087 mothers were administered word1 -- three times as many. So the 0/1 threshold applied upstream is demonstrably NOT the skip-logic threshold recorded in the instrument, and the agent was right to refuse an option label. This is a genuine data-provenance gap in the IL-HTE upstream dataset and is a candidate for its own GitHub issue; resolving it needs Gilbert's construction code, not another source.
